title: Modes: FM, SSB and CW
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: A mode is the way your voice, or your data, rides on a radio signal.
lines.label: modulation

lines.caption: FM changes the frequency of the signal. It is the mode of handheld radios and repeaters.
lines.label: FM

lines.caption: Single sideband is a slimmed-down form of amplitude modulation. It sends one sideband and nothing else.
lines.label: single sideband

lines.caption: CW is Morse code: the signal is simply switched on and off.
lines.say: C W is Morse code: the signal is simply switched on and off.
lines.label: CW

lines.caption: Each mode takes up a different amount of room on the band. That room is called bandwidth.
lines.label: bandwidth

lines.caption: CW is the narrowest. Single sideband is next, then FM. Television is the widest by far.
lines.say: C W is the narrowest. Single sideband is next, then F M. Television is the widest by far.
lines.label: narrow to wide
